config.title: Technical roadmapping

intro.title: Technical roadmapping
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple technical roadmap for a hypothetical software project, outlining key features, milestones, and timelines. You will learn the core concept of technical roadmapping, which involves planning and sequencing technical work to achieve strategic goals. The main constructs involved are defining objectives, breaking down tasks, and estimating timelines in a structured format. This exercise will help you understand how to translate product vision into actionable engineering plans. You will practice creating a clear, prioritized roadmap that aligns technical efforts with business needs.
intro.usecase: Technical roadmapping is a core leadership practice for aligning engineering efforts with business goals, appearing in product planning tools like Jira Roadmaps or GitHub Projects. It translates high-level strategy into actionable technical plans, such as a dashboard visualizing a quarterly migration from a monolith to microservices. Developers use these roadmaps to prioritize features, allocate resources, and communicate timelines, ensuring teams build the right things at the right time.

objectives: Construct a technical roadmap framework with defined phases and milestones
Apply prioritization matrices to evaluate and sequence technical initiatives
Configure dependency mapping between technical projects and business objectives
Integrate risk assessment protocols into roadmap planning processes
Manipulate timeline variables to model different implementation scenarios
Initialize stakeholder communication templates for roadmap presentations
Render visual roadmap artifacts that communicate technical strategy

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package to enable component creation and state management.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and hooks for a component
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have React and useState available for use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the Roadmap component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Roadmap that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Roadmap component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Roadmap component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The Roadmap component is created and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've defined the main Roadmap component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named Roadmap and returns a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is not defined correctly. Check the name and return statement.

steps.title: Initialize roadmap state
steps.instruction: Inside your Roadmap component, use useState to declare a state variable named roadmapItems initialized with an empty array.
steps.hint: Call useState with [] as the initial value and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a list
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a roadmapItems state variable ready to hold roadmap data.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty array initial value, and the state variable is named roadmapItems.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with [] and naming the variable roadmapItems.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing state. Use useState([]) to create a state variable called roadmapItems.

steps.title: Define addRoadmapItem handler
steps.instruction: Inside your Roadmap component, define a function named addRoadmapItem that takes title and description parameters and adds a new item to the roadmapItems state array.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setRoadmapItems state setter to add a new object with title and description properties to the existing array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component should now have an addRoadmapItem function that can add new roadmap items to the state.
successCriteria: A function named addRoadmapItem is defined that takes title and description parameters and updates the roadmapItems state with a new item object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your addRoadmapItem function properly updates the state by adding a new object with title and description properties to the existing array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addRoadmapItem function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function that takes title and description parameters and uses setRoadmapItems to add a new item to the state array.

steps.title: Define removeRoadmapItem handler
steps.instruction: Define a function called removeRoadmapItem that takes an index parameter and removes that item from the roadmapItems state array.
steps.hint: Use the setRoadmapItems function with the current state to filter out the item at the given index.
steps.expectedOutcome: The removeRoadmapItem function is defined and ready to be used for removing items from the roadmap.
successCriteria: A function named removeRoadmapItem is defined that takes an index parameter and updates the roadmapItems state by removing the item at that index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes an index parameter and uses setRoadmapItems to filter out the item at that index from the state array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeRoadmapItem function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function that removes an item from the roadmapItems state based on its index position.

steps.title: Add roadmap container structure
steps.instruction: In your Roadmap component's return statement, replace the current `null` with a container `<div>` that includes a `<header>` element with the text 'Technical Roadmap'.
steps.hint: Start by returning a `<div>` element, then place a `<header>` element inside it with the heading text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render a container with a header displaying 'Technical Roadmap'.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a `<div>` wrapping a `<header>` element with the text 'Technical Roadmap'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a `<div>` containing a `<header>` with the exact text 'Technical Roadmap'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure is missing or incorrect. The component should return a `<div>` with a `<header>` inside.

steps.title: Display roadmap items list
steps.instruction: Inside the Roadmap component's return, add a <ul> element that maps through the roadmapItems state array. For each item, render an <li> element containing the item's title and description.
steps.hint: Use the map method on roadmapItems to iterate. Each <li> should display both title and description properties from the item object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The roadmap items list will be rendered in the UI, displaying each item's title and description as list items.
successCriteria: A <ul> element is added that maps through roadmapItems, and each <li> displays both title and description from the item object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some list structure, but ensure you're mapping through roadmapItems and displaying both title and description for each item.
steps.feedbackWrong: The roadmap items list isn't displaying correctly. Check that you're using map on roadmapItems and rendering <li> elements with the item's title and description.

steps.title: Add form for new roadmap items
steps.instruction: Inside your Roadmap component's return statement, add a form element with two input fields (one for title, one for description) and a submit button labeled 'Add Item'.
steps.hint: Place the form above the existing roadmap items list. Use appropriate input types and labels for clarity.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: adding a form with inputs
<form>
  <label>Title: <input type="text" /></label>
  <label>Description: <input type="text" /></label>
  <button type="submit">Add Item</button>
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now include a form with title and description inputs and an 'Add Item' button, enabling users to input new roadmap items.
successCriteria: A form element with two labeled input fields and a submit button labeled 'Add Item' is added to the component's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some form elements, but make sure to include both title and description inputs and the 'Add Item' submit button.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form structure is missing or incomplete. Add a form with two input fields and a submit button labeled 'Add Item'.

steps.title: Wire form submission to add handler
steps.instruction: Add an onSubmit handler to the form that calls addRoadmapItem with the input values and prevents default form behavior.
steps.hint: Use the onSubmit attribute on the form element and call addRoadmapItem inside it. Remember to prevent the default form submission with e.preventDefault().
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will now properly submit new roadmap items when the Add Item button is clicked.
successCriteria: The form element has an onSubmit handler that calls addRoadmapItem with the input values and prevents default form behavior.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your onSubmit handler both prevents default form behavior and calls addRoadmapItem.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form submission isn't properly wired yet. Add an onSubmit handler to the form that calls addRoadmapItem and prevents default behavior.

steps.title: Add delete buttons to roadmap items
steps.instruction: Add a delete button to each roadmap item in the list and wire its onClick to call removeRoadmapItem with the item's id.
steps.hint: Inside the li element, add a button element with an onClick handler that calls removeRoadmapItem with item.id as the argument.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: adding a delete button to a list item
  • Item content
steps.expectedOutcome: Each roadmap item will have a delete button that removes it from the list when clicked.
successCriteria: Each li element contains a button with onClick that calls removeRoadmapItem with item.id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it's inside each li element and the onClick handler correctly calls removeRoadmapItem with item.id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The delete button is missing or not properly wired. Each roadmap item should have a button that calls removeRoadmapItem with the item's id when clicked.
